gates.reason: Malformed version strings can be accepted as patch releases, bypassing all release-gate checks.
This release-state script does not produce recommendation claims, provenance, validated fix snippets, or user-facing calculations governed by the data-integrity gate.
This is a manually/CI-invoked release utility, not hot-path or shipped runtime surface code.

findings.title: Non-anchored version parser permits release-gate bypass
findings.what: The version regular expression lacks an end anchor, so it accepts any string beginning with a valid-looking version. For example, `v0.2.1junk` is classified as patch 1; `main()` then exits successfully through the patch exemption before inspecting milestone gates. A malformed or unintended release target can therefore bypass the security and other standing release checks.
findings.fix: Require the entire normalized argument to match the supported version grammar by adding an end anchor: `/^(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?$/`.
findings.acceptance: Assert that `classifyTarget` rejects `v0.2.1junk`, `v0.2.1.0`, and `v0.2-beta`, while accepting documented forms such as `v0.2`, `0.2.0`, and `v0.2.1`; confirm invalid inputs exit non-zero before the patch exemption.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed line 55 performs a prefix-only match and lines 238-245 unconditionally exit 0 whenever the parsed patch is greater than zero. Thus `v0.2.1junk` deterministically reaches the exemption without any `gh` release-gate inspection.
